turns.query: Screen original Form N-MFP3 accessions with 2025 report dates and report-date net assets of at least $10 billion. Within each accession's report-date calendar month, order its reported liquidity observations by date and form consecutive steps. Retain steps whose weekly-liquid-asset amount and reported fraction are both positive at both endpoints. Rank by the most negative ending-minus-starting weekly-liquid-assets fraction, breaking a tie by earlier ending date, series name and accession. Report the eligible accession and step counts; selected accession, series, report date and net assets; step dates; both weekly-liquid-asset amounts and fractions; and decline-magnitude margin over the runner-up. Explain what the ranking actually picked out about this fund's reported liquid-asset share, and which other things it deliberately does not rank on.

claims.description: The response identifies the selected step as the largest decline in the reported weekly-liquid-assets fraction among the governed positive-observation population, rather than a ranking of fund size or shareholder flows.

turns.query: For the accession and ending date selected above, aggregate all reported share-class flow rows on that exact date. Report the contributing row count, gross subscriptions, gross redemptions, and net outflow, redemptions minus subscriptions, divided by report-date net assets. Also report net outflow divided by the turn-1 decline in weekly liquid assets. Explain how much of the drop in liquid assets the day's net redemptions can account for, and what each of those two figures actually measures.

claims.description: The response concludes from the computed amounts that the same-day net shareholder outflow explains only part of the reported weekly-liquid-assets decline, so the two changes do not form an accounting reconciliation.

The response distinguishes share-class subscriptions and redemptions from a reported portfolio-liquidity classification and treats the weekly-bucket decline as a classification change distinct from realized asset sales or settlement funding.

turns.query: Bracket the selected liquidity-step ending date with the immediately prior and immediately following CFTC report dates for the futures-only 3-month SOFR contract code 134741. For each endpoint calculate leveraged-money long minus short contracts. Report both dates, both net positions, their change, both open-interest levels and the open-interest change. Explain what this market-positioning overlay does and does not establish about the fund event.

claims.description: The response identifies from the signed results that leveraged-money positioning becomes more net short while aggregate open interest declines across the bracket.
The response explains that the weekly market-wide CFTC category is separate from the selected fund's portfolio classifications and shareholder flows, leaving any causal link unestablished.

turns.query: Decompose the turn-1 dollar change in weekly liquid assets. At both step endpoints report daily liquid assets; weekly liquid assets minus daily liquid assets is the other component. Compute the ending-minus-starting change in each component and report their summed change minus the reported weekly-liquid-assets change. Explain which component drives the drawdown and the scope of this additive bridge.

claims.description: The response identifies from the decomposition that the daily-liquid-assets bucket supplies almost all of the weekly-liquid-assets decline, while the weekly-minus-daily increment also decreases.

The response treats weekly minus daily liquid assets as an arithmetic residual between overlapping reported buckets, not as a separately reported security portfolio or independently liquidated balance.

judge_reference.source: Frozen SEC N-MFP filings/flows/liquidity and 2025 CFTC financial-futures reports
facts: Among 1,137 large original accessions and 22,383 positive consecutive steps, Columbia Short-Term Cash Fund accession 0001145549-25-006380 falls from 70.73% to 61.03% weekly liquid assets on 2025-01-30 to 2025-01-31.
The ending date has one flow row, a 0.775476 billion USD net outflow and a 2.534270 billion USD decline in reported weekly liquid assets; these movements do not reconcile.
The CFTC bracket is 2025-01-28 to 2025-02-04; leveraged-money net declines by 53,279 contracts and open interest declines by 8,865.
Daily liquid assets decline by 2.482902 billion USD and the weekly-minus-daily increment declines by 0.051368 billion, exactly decomposing the weekly-bucket change at source precision.
known_overclaims: Treating nonreported zero-liquidity rows as economic liquidation events.
Equating a reported liquidity-bucket change with shareholder flows or realized sales.
Attributing the fund event to aggregate CFTC positioning.
Calling weekly minus daily liquid assets a separately reported asset portfolio.
